pathway.title: COMMERCIAL METALS Co — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is the dominant constraint and it is new. Net leverage at 2026-05-31 was 2.47x and total debt 2.96x of reported EBITDA, after USD 2,000 million of senior unsecured notes and cash funded USD 2,516,122 thousand of acquisitions; at the 2025 year end net leverage was 0.71x, or 2.25x pro forma for the acquisition on 2025-12-01 and 4.90x pro forma for the acquisition on 2025-12-15. Basis: calculation M1; calculation M2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Business quality is the strongest support. The company is the largest U.S. rebar manufacturer and fabricator on its own description, runs scrap recycling, mills and fabrication as one chain, and North America Steel Group earned 77.7% of segment adjusted EBITDA; the integrated chain and a fabrication backlog give more visibility than a pure mill, though products are commodity-priced. Basis: calculation M9; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 11

- Cash generation is solid but heavily absorbed. Free cash flow of USD 405,038 thousand over the last twelve months is 0.35x of EBITDA after capital spending of USD 513,190 thousand, and about USD 550 million is planned for fiscal 2026 for the West Virginia mill, so deleveraging comes mainly from earnings growth rather than free cash flow. Basis: calculation M4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 48

- Liquidity is adequate near term but not a large surplus. Cash of USD 559,759 thousand and the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolver give USD 1,558,789 thousand committed, which is 1.10x the identified near-term claims of USD 1,413,168 thousand before any operating cash flow, with the revolver running to 2030-12-17. Basis: calculation M5; calculation M6; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

- Interest cover reads better than the run-rate. Cover on cash interest paid is 13.46x, but the new notes carry an annual coupon of USD 117,500 thousand and interest payable over the next twelve months is USD 170.9 million, so run-rate cover is 6.72x. Basis: calculation M3; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Financial policy is average: the board is independent and a leverage goal below 2x by mid-2027 is stated, but buybacks and a higher dividend continued while debt rose, and restricted payment capacity is not established. The litigation accrual of USD 373,476 thousand is 13.15% of net debt and sits outside debt. Basis: calculation M12; calculation M13; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: Strength: scale and integration. CMC reports net sales of USD 7,798,480 thousand and says it is the largest U.S. rebar manufacturer and fabricator, with recycling, mills and fabrication in one chain that secures scrap and keeps its mills loaded; this lowers input and demand risk compared with a stand-alone mill and supports cash generation through the cycle. Basis: calculation M9; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 13

Strength: trade protection and demand visibility. A 50% tariff on most steel imports supports domestic prices, and fabrication backlog of USD 845.7 million of remaining obligations with about 70% due within twelve months gives visibility for North America fabrication; this supports margin and cash flow while the tariff stands. Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 37

Strength: liquidity and market access. Cash of USD 559,759 thousand, an undrawn revolver of USD 1,000 million to 2030-12-17 and a USD 2,000 million note issue in November 2025 show lenders and the bond market funded a large acquisition programme; this lowers near-term refinancing risk. Basis: calculation M5; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 22

Strength: earnings recovery and precast contribution. Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 1,154,161 thousand over the last twelve months, a 13.04% margin, and precast added USD 86.5 million in nine months; this lifts debt service capacity if it persists. Basis: calculation M8; calculation M10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness: leverage after debt-funded acquisitions. Net leverage of 2.47x at 2026-05-31, against 0.71x at the 2025 year end, shrinks the cushion against a margin squeeze, and goodwill and intangibles are 81.9% of the allocated acquisition price, so little tangible value backs the new debt. Basis: calculation M1; calculation M13; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness: interest and capital spending absorb cash. Run-rate interest of USD 170.9 million and capital spending of about USD 550 million this year leave free cash flow at 0.35x of EBITDA and make deleveraging depend on earnings. Basis: calculation M3; calculation M4; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 50

Weakness: cyclical, commodity-priced earnings with policy exposure. Fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin was 5.65% (10.30% before the litigation charge) against 12.22% a year earlier, showing how quickly margin can compress when steel prices fall relative to scrap, and the tariff that supports prices could be relaxed. Basis: calculation M8; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 12

Weakness: litigation outside debt. The Pacific Steel Group judgment is accrued at USD 373,476 thousand with payment timing uncertain, and a second suit seeking about USD 29 million has no accrual; a cash payment would draw on liquidity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30

Opportunity: the fourth micro mill in West Virginia is due to start production in 2026 and the precast platform can grow with infrastructure demand, both of which would raise earnings if delivered; threat: tariff relaxation, import resurgence, integration problems and a rise in scrap or energy costs would each lower margin and cash flow. Basis: 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 12

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: CMC completed two cash acquisitions in December 2025 that created a precast platform: Concrete Pipe and Precast, LLC on 2025-12-01 for about USD 675 million from cash on hand, and the holding companies that own Foley Products Company, LLC on 2025-12-15 for about USD 1.84 billion. Foley was funded from the proceeds of the 2033 and 2035 senior unsecured notes, USD 1,000 million each, issued in November 2025, which raised net proceeds of USD 1,985,000 thousand. The purchase price allocations are preliminary and goodwill and intangibles are 81.9% of the allocated price. Basis: calculation K4; calculation K5; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–15; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 22

The notes add an annual coupon of USD 117,500 thousand, which is 68.8% of the USD 170.9 million of interest payable on long-term debt in the next twelve months, and the first coupons were paid on 2026-05-15 and 2026-06-15. In December 2025 the revolver was raised from USD 600.0 million to USD 1.0 billion and extended to 2030-12-17; a bridge facility of up to USD 1.85 billion and a backstop revolver of USD 600.0 million were committed in October 2025, and the sources do not state that either was drawn. Basis: calculation K7; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 116

fields.value: Financial foundation for COMMERCIAL METALS Co (cmc-22444), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is statements, debt, leverage, cover and liquidity for fiscal 2024, fiscal 2025 and the last twelve months to 2026-05-31, from the supplied annual and quarterly filings and results releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage reached 2.47x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-05-31 after debt-funded acquisitions, a much heavier claim on cash flow than before, though liquidity stays ample. Total debt is 2.96x EBITDA, and the acquisitions, USD 2,516,122 thousand net of cash acquired, contribute earnings only since December 2025, so a full-year view would show less leverage; the issuer's own adjusted figure is 2.1x.

fields.value: Interest cover of 13.46x on cash interest paid flatters the position because the new notes paid only part of a year of coupons; against interest payable over the next twelve months, cover is 6.72x. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage on reported EBITDA moved from 0.34x at the 2024 year end to 0.71x at the 2025 year end and 2.47x at 2026-05-31, and the rise comes from debt rather than weaker earnings. The 2025 year-end net debt of USD 311,043 thousand is not like-for-like: pro forma net debt is USD 986,043 thousand (2.25x) after the Concrete Pipe and Precast acquisition on 2025-12-01 and USD 2,151,043 thousand (4.90x) after the Foley acquisition on 2025-12-15, each on year-end EBITDA that holds none of the acquired earnings. Creditors therefore hold a far larger claim at 2026-05-31, with net debt of USD 2,840,726 thousand, supported by earnings that have absorbed the precast businesses for less than six months.

fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-05-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 92

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage is strong on its face but overstated. Cash interest paid over the last twelve months was USD 85,268 thousand, giving cover of 13.46x, yet the 2033 and 2035 senior unsecured notes, USD 2,000,000 thousand in total, were issued in November 2025 and paid only part of a year of coupons. Interest payable over the next twelve months is USD 170.9 million, which puts run-rate cover at 6.72x on reported EBITDA that itself includes the acquisitions only from December 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash-flow quality is adequate but not yet strong. Operating cash flow of USD 918,228 thousand over the last twelve months less capital expenditures of USD 513,190 thousand leaves free cash flow of USD 405,038 thousand, or 0.35x EBITDA, and nine months of working capital absorbed USD 195,098 thousand, which the issuer attributes to higher materials costs in inventories and higher selling prices in receivables. Capital spending of about USD 550 million is planned for fiscal 2026, driven by the fourth micro mill in West Virginia, so free cash flow stays well below operating cash flow while that build continues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity covers the visible near-term claims. Cash of USD 559,759 thousand and the undrawn revolver, available after USD 1.0 million of letters of credit, give committed liquidity of USD 1,558,789 thousand, and USD 1,768,475 thousand on the issuer's wider basis, against current maturities of USD 88,792 thousand, a litigation accrual of USD 373,476 thousand whose payment timing is uncertain, and purchase obligations of about USD 780 million due within twelve months. The revolver of USD 1,000 million matures on 2030-12-17.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strongest contrary evidence is the issuer's own message that leverage is falling toward less than 2x ahead of its mid-2027 goal, supported by core EBITDA margin of 14.2% in the latest quarter and expected annualized precast EBITDA of USD 245 million that its 2.1x measure includes. That view would win if the fiscal 2026 results show a full year of precast earnings, free cash flow near the current run-rate and cash used to repay debt; it would lose if the litigation accrual is paid in cash or capital spending stays high, because net debt would then rise rather than fall.

fields.value: Business and governance facts for COMMERCIAL METALS Co (cmc-22444), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and capital allocation behaviour, and the 2025 and 2026 acquisitions and new debt, from the supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CMC remains a cyclical, vertically integrated steel and construction-products group, but its credit profile now rests on integrating two debt-funded precast acquisitions that changed the company more than any operating shift did. Precast delivered adjusted EBITDA of USD 86.5 million in nine months, and the issuer's 2.1x net leverage reproduces at 2.12x from its own inputs, which corrects the Financial foundation statement that it could not be reproduced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The shareholder base is listed and widely held with no controlling holder identified, and nine of ten directors are independent; the proxy statement that would confirm control rights is not supplied. Dividends rose 11% in March 2026 and buybacks of USD 76.1 million continued alongside USD 2,000 million of new notes, so creditor alignment rests on the stated aim of leverage below 2x by mid-2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The precast acquisitions are the dominant credit event, and they were mostly debt-funded: Foley, the larger purchase, was paid from the 2033 and 2035 senior unsecured notes, whose net proceeds equal 78.9% of the USD 2,516,122 thousand of cash paid net of cash acquired for both purchases, and Concrete Pipe and Precast was paid from cash on hand. Goodwill and intangibles make up 81.9% of the allocated price, so little tangible asset value stands behind the new debt, and the businesses added net sales of USD 320.3 million and pre-tax earnings of USD 24,625 thousand since closing.

fields.value: - The legacy base is cyclical but integrated and, for now, supported by trade policy. North America Steel Group supplies 75.1% of net sales and 77.7% of segment adjusted EBITDA in nine months, its metal margin per ton rose 27%, and a 50% tariff on most steel imports props up domestic prices; relaxation of that tariff is the main external risk to the margin.

Net debt of USD 2,865,703 thousand on the issuer's definition over adjusted EBITDA adjusted for expected annualized precast EBITDA of USD 245 million gives 2.12x, so the 2.1x depends on that management expectation rather than on reported precast results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership and governance look conventional for a listed company but control rights are not established. The board has ten directors with nine independent and a separate chairman, and the auditor has served for decades, yet the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indentures are not supplied, so holders above five percent, restricted payment capacity and guarantor scope are not known; the sponsor and governance risk level is medium on that evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder returns continued while debt rose. Buybacks and dividends took USD 138,234 thousand in nine months, 22.9% of operating cash flow, and the dividend was raised 11% in March 2026; this is moderate in size but is discretionary cash that could repay debt after a debt-funded acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Litigation is the main event risk outside debt. A jury verdict of USD 110.0 million for Pacific Steel Group, trebled by the court, is accrued at USD 373,476 thousand in current liabilities with payment timing uncertain, and a second suit seeking about USD 29 million has no accrual; the company is appealing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disclosure is frequent and reconciled, with one correction. The latest quarterly report corrected pro forma net sales that the second-quarter report overstated by USD 75.1 million, which the company judged not material; reported statements were not affected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a more levered, integration-dependent view is operating momentum and the issuer's own path: core EBITDA margin of 14.2% in the latest quarter, precast adjusted EBITDA of USD 86.5 million in nine months against a management expectation of USD 245 million annualized, and a stated aim of leverage below 2x ahead of mid-2027. That view would win if fiscal 2026 results show a full year of precast earnings near the expectation, free cash flow applied to debt rather than buybacks, and the tariff intact. It would lose if the Pacific Steel Group accrual of USD 373,476 thousand is paid in cash, if the tariff is relaxed and margins narrow, or if integration costs and capital spending for the West Virginia mill stay high.

fields.value: Strength: scale and integration. CMC reports net sales of USD 7,798,480 thousand and says it is the largest U.S. rebar manufacturer and fabricator, with recycling, mills and fabrication in one chain that secures scrap and keeps its mills loaded; this lowers input and demand risk compared with a stand-alone mill and supports cash generation through the cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: trade protection and demand visibility. A 50% tariff on most steel imports supports domestic prices, and fabrication backlog of USD 845.7 million of remaining obligations with about 70% due within twelve months gives visibility for North America fabrication; this supports margin and cash flow while the tariff stands.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: liquidity and market access. Cash of USD 559,759 thousand, an undrawn revolver of USD 1,000 million to 2030-12-17 and a USD 2,000 million note issue in November 2025 show lenders and the bond market funded a large acquisition programme; this lowers near-term refinancing risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: earnings recovery and precast contribution. Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 1,154,161 thousand over the last twelve months, a 13.04% margin, and precast added USD 86.5 million in nine months; this lifts debt service capacity if it persists.

fields.value: Weakness: interest and capital spending absorb cash. Run-rate interest of USD 170.9 million and capital spending of about USD 550 million this year leave free cash flow at 0.35x of EBITDA and make deleveraging depend on earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: cyclical, commodity-priced earnings with policy exposure. Fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin was 5.65% (10.30% before the litigation charge) against 12.22% a year earlier, showing how quickly margin can compress when steel prices fall relative to scrap, and the tariff that supports prices could be relaxed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: litigation outside debt. The Pacific Steel Group judgment is accrued at USD 373,476 thousand with payment timing uncertain, and a second suit seeking about USD 29 million has no accrual; a cash payment would draw on liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunity: the fourth micro mill in West Virginia is due to start production in 2026 and the precast platform can grow with infrastructure demand, both of which would raise earnings if delivered; threat: tariff relaxation, import resurgence, integration problems and a rise in scrap or energy costs would each lower margin and cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CMC is a vertically integrated North American and Polish steel and construction-products group that recycles scrap, melts it in electric arc furnaces, rolls rebar, merchant bar and wire rod, and fabricates reinforcing steel; since December 2025 it also makes precast concrete and pipe products. Net sales were USD 7,798,480 thousand in fiscal 2025, 79.7% of them in the United States, and North America Steel Group supplied 78.0% of external net sales and 77.7% of segment adjusted EBITDA in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, so the credit rests mainly on U.S. rebar economics. The business is cyclical, seasonal and commodity-priced, with net sales higher in the third and fourth quarters, which makes interim leverage swing with the season.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M9; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-08-31_cmc.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is listed with no controlling holder identified, nine of ten directors independent and a separate chairman, so there is no sponsor to extract or support and creditor alignment rests on the board and stated policy. Dividends and buybacks continued after the acquisitions, the financial policy is average, and the proxy statement, credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so ownership above five percent, restricted payment capacity and guarantor scope are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is driven by steel price and tons shipped. In nine months to 2026-05-31 North America steel products metal margin per ton rose 27% and tons shipped fell 3%, so earnings came from price spread rather than volume, which is more reversible; precast adds infrastructure-oriented products whose cyclicality is not yet shown in the sources, and fabrication backlog gives visibility only in North America. Customer concentration is not disclosed, so durability beyond that backlog is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins depend on the spread between selling prices and scrap, plus power and gas, which are partly hedged; the adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.22% in fiscal 2024, 5.65% in fiscal 2025 (10.30% before the litigation charge) and 13.04% over the last twelve months, so margin has moved by several percentage points within two years. Operating leverage is high because mills run at high fixed cost, so a volume or spread decline passes quickly to EBITDA and then to free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is moderate: capital spending is 5.80% of last-twelve-months net sales, free cash flow is 0.35x of EBITDA, and nine months of working capital absorbed USD 195,098 thousand as inventory costs and selling prices rose; capital spending is partly discretionary once the West Virginia mill is finished, which gives some flexibility over the maturity wall that begins with USD 300,000 thousand of notes due in January 2030.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high and the main force on margin: the 2025 annual report describes global steelmaking capacity far above demand and import competition, so price takers lose margin first when imports return; buyer power is moderate because fabricated rebar is generally sold through competitive bids, often on fixed-price projects; supplier power is moderate because scrap and energy prices swing, partly offset by company-owned recycling; new entrants are limited by the capital needed for a mill and substitutes for rebar are few. The tariff and the European carbon border mechanism are the policy factors that matter to credit: the tariff supports U.S. margin and its removal is the largest external risk, while the European mechanism improved Polish volumes and carbon cost assistance of USD 36.0 million was received in nine months against USD 48.1 million a year earlier, so Europe Steel Group earnings partly depend on government payments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are strong: net sales of USD 7,798,480 thousand and a self-described leading position in U.S. rebar give shock absorption. Competitive advantage is average: integration and cost position help, but products are commodity-priced and margin relies on tariffs. Business diversification is average: North America Steel Group is 75.1% of net sales in nine months and the United States 79.7% of fiscal 2025 sales, with precast and Europe adding limited offset. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital spending is 5.80% of last-twelve-months net sales and part of it ends when the West Virginia mill is finished, but power-intensive mills carry high fixed cost. Margin stability is weak: adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.22%, 5.65% and 13.04% across fiscal 2024, fiscal 2025 and the last twelve months. Free cash flow stability is average: it was USD 575,437 thousand, USD 312,249 thousand and USD 405,038 thousand in the same periods, positive but variable. Ability to refinance is average: USD 2,000 million of notes were placed in November 2025 and the first large maturity is in January 2030, but ratings are not stated. Liquidity is average: committed liquidity of USD 1,558,789 thousand covers identified near-term claims 1.10x before operating cash flow. Financial policy and governance are average: independent board and a stated leverage goal, offset by continued buybacks and a higher dividend while leverage rose; these are analyst assessments, not ratings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M4; calculation M5; calculation M6; calculation M8; calculation M9; calculation M11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over twelve to twenty-four months the issuer expects the fourth quarter core EBITDA to rise sequentially, a mill outage headwind of about USD 20 million to fall away and precast to add; leverage should fall if precast earns its expected USD 245 million a year, but this is management's view and is not confirmed by any later document. Over three to five years the West Virginia mill and precast platform lift capacity and diversification, while the company plans leverage below 2x by mid-2027, so the medium-term credit trend is improving if delivery follows, with the tariff and construction cycle as the swing factors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside begins with a relaxation of import protection or a construction slowdown that narrows steel prices against scrap, and mills first lose margin per ton; as legacy earnings fall back to the fiscal 2025 level before the litigation charge, EBITDA drops while interest of USD 170.9 million a year, capital spending and the litigation accrual do not. On net debt at 2026-05-31, net leverage would be 3.54x on that earnings level and 2.71x if precast reaches USD 245 million, so free cash flow falls toward zero, buybacks would have to stop and the company would draw first on cash of USD 559,759 thousand and then on the undrawn revolver. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, because committed liquidity is 1.10x the identified near-term claims before operating cash flow, but covenant headroom is not established, and the observable triggers are metal margin per ton, tariff changes, free cash flow and the pace of buybacks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, CMC presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, integration and domestic leadership, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that rose to 2.47x after debt-funded acquisitions, run-rate interest cover of 6.72x and a litigation accrual outside debt. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is positive but absorbed by capital spending, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of precast earnings and on the tariff, with the first large maturity of USD 300,000 thousand in January 2030. The primary downside path is a margin squeeze in U.S. steel while interest, capital spending and litigation stay fixed. Further analysis would require covenant headroom at 2026-05-31, the credit agreement and indentures, agency ratings and fiscal 2026 results. Top risk: leverage after debt-funded acquisitions combined with margin cyclicality.
